findings.title: Report unreadable corpus path as UNVERIFIABLE
findings.text: This `expect` aborts with exit 101 when the resolved root is not valid UTF-8, which breaks `bench`'s exit contract (0/1/3) and the three-state rule that an unreadable corpus is reported as UNVERIFIABLE, never folded into a panic. Convert the path first and fall into the same `[UNVERIFIABLE]`/`return 3` branch already used for a load failure; the registry `to_str().expect(...)` just below has the same problem.

findings.title: Return an error instead of panicking
findings.text: The doc comment promises that "a caller that cannot load it reports UNVERIFIABLE", but this `expect` panics on a non-UTF-8 `root` instead of returning `Err`, so `canon` can never surface that degradation. Since the function already returns `Result<Registry, String>`, try the conversion and return the error with the offending path so the caller's UNVERIFIABLE path is reached.

findings.title: Make exponent overflow deterministic
findings.text: `i64::pow` inherits overflow checks, so a large `power` panics under the debug/`nextest` gate but wraps silently in a release build — two different scaling factors on a canonicalization path, i.e. an address that depends on the profile. Use `checked_pow` so overflow fails identically everywhere (or reject the exponent where it is parsed) rather than producing a wrapped factor in release.
